survey: A palm tree on a sand dune. The trunk comes up out of the sand at the lower center, curving slightly left and then right as it rises. The camera is a little above the ground, so we see the top of the sand, with pebbles lying on it and the frond shadow cast across it to the right. The trunk's ring segments are shallow downward curves that wrap around a round trunk, which fits that slightly high viewpoint. They narrow steadily as the trunk tapers, and they turn with the trunk's bend. Two coconuts hang in a cluster where the trunk meets the crown and partly overlap each other. The fronds spread out from the crown and arch down. We see their upper surfaces from the side and slightly above, and their spread fits the trunk's top. The trunk base sinks into the sand with a soft mound around it, and that mound matches the angle of the ground. Every part of the drawing agrees on one gentle three-quarter view from slightly above.
